arguments.objective:
Implement a dependency-free Node.js ESM project planner in the shared workspace. This is a multi-module project: create cli.mjs, lib/store.mjs for JSON persistence and input-safe writes, and lib/planner.mjs for project/task/domain rules. Keep the modules cohesive; no reference implementation is available in the initial workspace. The complete immutable contract is in acceptance/planner.md and the frozen acceptance/planner.test.mjs. Never edit acceptance/ or any test file.

The CLI has project add/list/report and task add/list/depend/ready/complete commands. PLAN_FILE selects storage; successful commands print one JSON value. Reject invalid commands without changing persisted bytes. IDs, dependency validation including cycle rejection, readiness, completion, reporting, and store isolation must satisfy the frozen contract. Do not access another experiment workspace.

Use at most five fresh implementation rounds. The following stages deliberately expose real failures in the unchanged full suite. Both controllers receive these exact instructions, identical initial acceptance files, the same model, the same preset, and the same five-round bound. The Custom controller has separate implementation and test children; the official controller has one worker per round. Every test role or official worker must execute the FULL suite once per round with `TODO_CLI="$PWD/cli.mjs" node --test --test-reporter=tap acceptance/planner.test.mjs`, report the actual pass/fail counts and exit code, and never filter or alter tests. The Custom host independently runs the same suite after its test child. The final outside evaluation uses a frozen copy.

Round 1: implement project add/list and task add/list with persistence, ID validation, literal text, and isolation. Leave task depend/ready/complete and project report unsupported with a nonzero exit status. Run/report the full suite; continue after its genuine failures.

Round 2: inspect the Round 1 workspace and failure handoff, then implement task depend and task ready, including duplicate, self, cross-project, and cycle rejection. Leave task complete and project report unsupported. Run/report the full suite; continue after its genuine failures.

Round 3: inspect the previous work and failures, then implement task complete and project report while preserving earlier behavior. Run/report the full suite. If any tests still fail, repair them in later rounds within the five-round cap. Return complete only after the entire unchanged suite passes. A planned intermediate failure is never a final success, and an assertion failure is not an infrastructure blocker.
